title: Understand syllabus
goal: Know exactly what the GATE DA paper covers and how it is marked, and turn the official syllabus into your own checklist.
activities: Read the official syllabus on the Syllabus page, subject by subject, and sort each phrase into new to you, studied but not practised, or comfortable.

Learn the paper's structure and marking: 65 questions in 180 minutes for 100 marks; MCQ, MSQ and NAT questions; negative marks only for wrong MCQ answers. The strategy article on MCQ, MSQ and NAT sets the rules out with the worked arithmetic.
Look at the Weightage page to see how marks were distributed across subjects in the official DA papers, remembering that it describes past papers and does not predict the next one.
Browse one official paper on the PYQs page to see the style and depth of the questions (read only, if you want to keep it for a timed attempt later).
Take a short baseline: one small untimed Practice set per subject, including General Aptitude, so that Progress and the Syllabus page have starting data.
Choose a subject order and a weekly routine (see the syllabus-completion strategy article), and start each study day from Today.
exitCriteria: Progress shows at least one scored attempt in every DA subject and in General Aptitude.
On the Syllabus page, your baseline attempts appear against at least one topic in every subject.
Your Bookmarks list holds the syllabus-completion and MCQ, MSQ and NAT strategy articles for quick reference.

title: Build fundamentals
goal: Learn every syllabus topic from first principles, concepts and formulas together, before heavy question practice.
activities: Work through each topic's notes in the Concept library: definition, intuition, the mathematics, the worked example and the common mistakes.
For each topic, read its entries in the Formula book, then write each formula and its conditions from memory once.
Finish each topic with a short untimed Practice set filtered to that topic, and read the detailed solution of every question, including the ones you got right.
Add the concepts and formulas you cannot yet recall to Revision, and clear Today's revision each day.
Give every Error log entry a mistake type and a one-line note on what would have prevented it.
Use Today for a daily concept, five formulas and the revision due.
exitCriteria: On the Syllabus page, every topic shows practice attempts; none is at zero.
On the Syllabus page, no topic reads "Not enough data" under Your topic mastery (each has at least three scored attempts).
Revision holds concept and formula items from every subject, and none of them is overdue.
Every entry in the Error log has a mistake type.

title: Complete topic-wise practice
goal: Make each topic reliable through focused practice until your accuracy is steady and your mistakes are understood.
activities: Run Practice sets filtered by subject and topic, mixing difficulty levels: untimed at first, then timed.
Use the Previously incorrect status on Practice (or the Retry what you got wrong quick set) to re-solve your mistakes from scratch.
Pace topic sets with the Subject practice mode of the Exam timer.
Check topic performance on Progress each week and move the weakest topics to the front of next week's plan.
Work through the Weak topics and Incorrect questions queues in Revision.
Move Error log entries from Open to Revising to Resolved as you fix each mistake, marking Resolved only after fresh correct attempts.
exitCriteria: On the Syllabus page, every topic's mastery reads Developing or better (a suggested target; mastery is a platform metric, not an official measure).
The count shown on Practice for Retry what you got wrong is falling from week to week.
The Error log has no Conceptual mistake entry still Open after two weeks (a suggested threshold).
Progress shows your accuracy for every subject and topic you have studied.

title: Solve PYQs
goal: Work through the official GATE DA papers to learn the paper's style, depth and traps, keeping a paper back for a timed run if you choose to.
activities: Decide whether to keep one official paper unseen for a timed simulation later; if you do, filter out that year when browsing PYQs.
Solve PYQs topic-wise: Practice with source Official PYQs and status Unattempted, or the PYQ browser filtered by subject and topic.
Attempt each question before opening its solution, and record your confidence before checking.
Read the option analysis and the common trap for every question, including the ones you got right.
Reattempt wrong, guessed and slow PYQs from the PYQs to reattempt queue in Revision.
Compare where your attempts are with the Weightage page, as a check that no subject is neglected.
exitCriteria: Subjects shows every official PYQ attempted in each subject, apart from any paper you deliberately held back.
On the Syllabus page, every topic that has official PYQs shows PYQ attempts.
Every question in the PYQs to reattempt queue in Revision has been reattempted at least once.
Every PYQ you got wrong has an Error log entry with a mistake type.

title: First revision
goal: Consolidate everything covered so far with one complete pass of spaced, active revision.
activities: Clear Today's revision every day, grading each item honestly as Forgot, Almost or Got it.
Work through the Weak topics and Frequently forgotten queues, relearning the concept behind any repeated failure.
Revise the Formula book one subject at a time from memory, marking any formula you hesitate on.
Re-solve the Incorrect questions queue from scratch.
Filter the Error log by mistake type, reread your one-line fixes, and update each entry's status.
Reread the Concept library notes for any topic whose mastery reads Needs work.
exitCriteria: Revision shows no overdue items, and Today's revision is cleared at the end of each study day.
On the Syllabus page, no topic's mastery reads Needs work.
No Error log entry is still Open; each is Revising or Resolved.
The Frequently forgotten queue in Revision is shorter than when you started this stage.

title: Mixed practice
goal: Learn to recognise what a question needs when subjects are mixed, as they are in the real paper, and start working against the clock.
activities: Use the Timed mixed drill quick set on Practice (30 questions across all subjects, against the clock).
Build shuffled sets across all subjects with source Both and status Unattempted.

Take the mixed Foundation mocks (8–10) and the Beginner → Intermediate mocks (11–20) as short mixed papers. Foundation mocks 1–7 each cover a single subject, and none of mocks 1–20 includes General Aptitude, so keep GA practice going alongside them.
For every question, decide early whether to solve it now, mark it for later or leave it, and compare each decision with the outcome afterwards.
Track your time per question on Progress against your budget (180 minutes for 100 marks averages 1.8 minutes per mark).
Classify every mistake from mixed sets in the Error log, watching especially for Misread question entries.
exitCriteria: Progress shows several timed mixed sessions with accuracy stable or rising.
Your time per question on Progress is close to the budget you set (a suggested reference is about 1.8 minutes per mark).
In your recent mock results, the Time sinks list is shorter than in your first mixed mocks.
New Misread question entries in the Error log have become rare.

title: Mock tests
goal: Build exam temperament with progressively longer timed mocks, and analyse each one thoroughly before taking the next.
activities: Take the Intermediate and Advanced mocks under exam conditions: no pauses, no notes, rough sheets and an on-screen calculator.
After each mock, follow the post-mock analysis loop: review every section of the results, classify each question and choose two or three priorities.
Read the time-management articles in Strategy and test one change at a time: order of attack, number of passes or checkpoints.
Set checkpoints in the Exam timer that match your plan, and check them during each mock.
Classify every mock mistake in the Error log and look closely at the Wrong with high confidence list.
Do focused Practice sets on the weak topics each mock reveals before taking the next one.
exitCriteria: Every mock you have taken has had its question review worked through, with no wrong or skipped question left unexamined.
In recent mock results, the Marked for review, never answered list is empty or holds only deliberate skips.
The Negative marking panel shows the marks lost to wrong MCQs falling, or holding at a level you have chosen to accept.
Progress shows your score trend across mocks of the same tier.

title: Advanced revision
goal: Close the specific gaps your mocks have exposed and deepen the topics where you still lose marks.
activities: Start from the Repeatedly wrong across your history list in your recent mock results, and relearn each topic on it.
Work through the Weak topics and High-weight topics queues in Revision, remembering that high weight is a historical observation, not a prediction.
Do Practice sets at the harder difficulty levels on topics where you are already Developing or Proficient.
Drill formula conditions from the Formula book: sample vs population variance, logarithm bases, 0- vs 1-based indexing, strict vs non-strict inequalities.
Reattempt everything in the PYQs to reattempt queue from scratch.
Reread the Error log by mistake type and turn the most common fixes into a short personal checklist.
exitCriteria: Topics flagged as weak in your recent mocks show improved accuracy on Progress.
The Frequently forgotten queue in Revision is shrinking.
No Error log entry from a mock is still Open.
On the Syllabus page, most topics read Proficient or Strong (a suggested target, not an official measure).

title: Full simulations
goal: Rehearse the complete 180-minute, 65-question paper until your pacing, question selection and decision rules are stable.
activities: Take the Full GATE-style simulations (Mocks 41–50, as they become available) at the time of day of your exam session.
If you held back an official paper, sit it as a timed 180-minute run from its page in PYQs, with the Exam timer in Full exam mode.
Settle your order of attack, number of passes and checkpoints, and save the checkpoints in the Exam timer.
Use the rough-work layout and on-screen calculator habits you will use on exam day.
Complete the full post-mock analysis after each simulation before taking the next.
Between simulations, do focused Practice and Revision on what each one exposed.
exitCriteria: Mock tests shows several full simulations completed and analysed (three or more is a suggested minimum).
In your recent full simulations, you reached each checkpoint within a few minutes of plan.
In recent results, Skipped questions holds only deliberate skips and Marked for review, never answered is empty.
Progress shows your full-simulation scores stable or rising rather than swinging widely.

title: Final revision
goal: Keep everything fresh, avoid opening new gaps, and arrive at the exam rested with a settled plan.
activities: Start each day from Today and clear Today's revision.
Go through the Formula book one subject at a time from memory; print it if working on paper helps you.
Reread your Error log fixes, your personal checklist and the items saved in Bookmarks.
Keep your pace with short timed Practice sets rather than starting large new topics.
Reread the exam-day strategy articles (first pass, question selection, MCQ, MSQ and NAT) and write your exam plan on one page.
Check the official GATE 2027 website (linked on the Sources page) for your admit card, exam centre, session and exam-day instructions.
exitCriteria: Revision shows no overdue items.
No Error log entry is still Open.
On the Syllabus page, no topic's mastery reads Needs work.
The checkpoints saved in the Exam timer match the plan you will use on exam day.
